Applying Digital Methods to Your Research

Lesson 2: Activity: Your Research Questions and Research Objects

Step 1: Your Research Questions

Let’s think about some of your past research projects. What were the research questions or objectives that guided those projects?

On a sheet of paper, write 2-4 research questions or sentences for projects that you have already completed. These should not be new projects, but ones that you have conducted and written about in the past.

Your research questions:

We will come back to these questions in a later section.

Step 2: Your Research Objects

Now that you have thought about some past projects, what were some of the research objects or resources that you used to conduct that research project? What objects did you analyze?

Research Objects

A research object can be something large like a whole book or website, or it can be something very small like a chart, line of poetry, or journal entry. If you are having trouble thinking of the scale by which you want to analyze, return to your research questions.

On the same sheet of paper, choose up to 5 objects that you have worked with in the past.

  • These objects can be very important to your research agenda or the first 5 items in your archival materials
  • If you have a range of media types (print media, digital files, audio, etc.) choose a range of types that are representative of your materials.
  • If you get stuck, look back at the projects you outlined in the previous section. They may jog your memory.
